¹ This is the oracle concerning Nineveh — the vision of Nahum of Elkosh. ² God is a jealous God who takes vengeance; the LORD takes vengeance and burns with fury. The LORD takes vengeance on his enemies and stores up wrath for those who oppose him. ³ The LORD is slow to anger but immense in power; he will by no means leave the guilty unpunished. His path is in the whirlwind and the storm, and the clouds are the dust beneath his feet. ⁴ He rebukes the sea and dries it up; he drains all the rivers. Bashan and Carmel wither; the blossoms of Lebanon fade. ⁵ The mountains tremble before him, the hills dissolve; the earth heaves at his presence — the world and all who live in it.

⁶ Who can endure his rage? Who can survive the heat of his anger? His fury pours out like fire; the rocks shatter before him. ⁷ The LORD is good — a refuge in times of trouble — and he knows those who trust in him. ⁸ But with a sweeping flood he will make a complete end of Nineveh; darkness will pursue his enemies. ⁹ What are you plotting against the LORD? He will make a complete end of it; trouble will not rise up a second time. ¹⁰ Like tangled thorns, like drunkards soaked in wine, they will be consumed like dry stubble.

¹¹ From you, Nineveh, came one who plotted evil against the LORD — a wicked schemer. ¹² This is what the LORD says: Although the Assyrians are strong and numerous, they will be cut down and swept away. Although I have afflicted you, Judah, I will afflict you no more. ¹³ Now I will break their yoke from your neck and tear away your chains. ¹⁴ And the LORD has issued a decree against you, Nineveh: your name will be perpetuated no longer. I will destroy the carved idols and cast metal images in the temple of your gods; I will prepare your grave, for you are despicable. ¹⁵ Look! On the mountains, the feet of one who brings good news — who announces peace! Celebrate your festivals, Judah; fulfill your vows. The wicked will never invade you again; they are completely destroyed.

¹ The attacker advances against Nineveh. Guard the fortress! Watch the road! Brace yourselves! Marshal all your strength! ² For the LORD will restore the splendor of Jacob, like the splendor of Israel, though enemies have plundered and devastated their vines. ³ The shields of the warriors are red; the soldiers are dressed in scarlet. The metal on the chariots flashes on the day of battle; the spears of juniper are brandished. ⁴ The chariots race madly through the streets, rushing back and forth through the squares, looking like torches, darting about like lightning. ⁵ The king summons his finest troops; they stumble as they march. They rush to the city wall; the siege canopy is set in place.

⁶ The river gates are flung open and the palace collapses. ⁷ The queen is stripped and carried away; her slave girls moan like doves, beating their breasts. ⁸ Nineveh is like a pool of water, but now its waters are draining away. "Stop! Stop!" they cry, but no one turns back. ⁹ Plunder the silver! Plunder the gold! There is no end to the treasure — an abundance of every precious thing. ¹⁰ Nineveh is empty, plundered, stripped bare! Hearts melt, knees give way, bodies tremble, every face grows pale.

¹¹ Where now is the lions' den — that feeding ground of the young lions — where the lion and lioness prowled, where the lion's cubs moved about with no one to frighten them? ¹² The lion tore apart prey enough for his cubs and strangled game for his mates; he filled his lairs with prey and his dens with plunder. ¹³ "I am against you," declares the LORD Almighty. "I will burn your chariots in smoke; the sword will devour your young lions. I will cut off your prey from the earth, and the voices of your messengers will be heard no more."

¹ Woe to the city of blood — full of lies, full of plunder, never without victims! ² The crack of the whip, the clatter of wheels, the galloping horses, the jolting chariots! ³ Charging cavalry, flashing swords, gleaming spears — a multitude of casualties, heaps of corpses, bodies without number — people stumble over the dead. ⁴ All because of the wanton lust of a prostitute, alluring and skilled in sorcery, who enslaved nations with her prostitution and peoples with her witchcraft. ⁵ "I am against you," declares the LORD Almighty. "I will lift your skirts over your face. I will show the nations your nakedness and the kingdoms your shame."

⁶ I will pelt you with filth and treat you with contempt; I will make you a spectacle. ⁷ All who see you will recoil and say, 'Nineveh is in ruins — who will mourn for her?' Where can I find anyone to comfort you? ⁸ Are you any better than Thebes, situated on the Nile, with water surrounding her? The river was her defense, the water her wall. ⁹ Cush and Egypt were her boundless strength; Put and Libya were among her allies. ¹⁰ Yet she was taken captive and went into exile. Her infants were dashed to pieces at every street corner. Lots were cast for her nobles, and all her great men were put in chains.

¹¹ You too will become drunk; you will go into hiding and seek refuge from the enemy. ¹² All your fortresses are like fig trees with their first ripe figs — when they are shaken, the figs fall into the mouth of the eater. ¹³ Look at your troops — they are all women! The gates of your land are wide open to your enemies; fire has consumed the bars of your gate. ¹⁴ Draw water for the siege; strengthen your defenses! Work the clay and tread the mortar; repair the brickwork! ¹⁵ There the fire will consume you; the sword will cut you down. Multiply like the locust, multiply like the swarm of locusts!

¹⁶ You have increased the number of your merchants until they outnumber the stars in the sky. But like locusts they strip the land and then fly away. ¹⁷ Your guards are like locusts, your officials like swarms of insects that settle in the walls on a cold day — but when the sun appears they fly away, and no one knows where they have gone. ¹⁸ King of Assyria, your shepherds slumber; your nobles lie down to rest. Your people are scattered on the mountains with no one to gather them. ¹⁹ Nothing can heal your wound; your injury is fatal. Everyone who hears the news about you claps their hands at your fall — for who has not been crushed again and again by your endless cruelty?
